item.title: EU leaders meet in Belgium to counter economic pressure from U.S. and China
item.description:
European Union leaders gathered Thursday at the historic Alden Biesen castle in eastern Belgium for an informal retreat aimed at revitalizing the bloc's stagnating economy and forging a united response to mounting pressure from the United States, China, and Russia.

The summit, convened by European Council President António Costa, comes as the 27-member bloc grapples with U.S. President Donald Trump's tariff threats, Chinese export restrictions on critical minerals, and hybrid threats from Moscow. Former Italian Prime Ministers Mario Draghi and Enrico Letta have been invited to present updates on their landmark 2024 reports on EU competitiveness and the single market.

item.title: Nissan narrows operating loss forecast as turnaround gains traction
item.description:
Nissan announced Thursday it expects a net loss of 650 billion yen ($4.2 billion) for fiscal year 2025 ending in March, as the Japanese automaker continues its sweeping turnaround effort under new leadership. The loss is driven primarily by non-cash charges tied to restructuring under the company's "Re:Nissan" recovery plan.

The forecast marks a difficult but potentially stabilizing chapter for Japan's third-largest carmaker, which has been battered by an aging vehicle lineup, intensifying competition from Chinese rivals, and the financial impact of U.S. tariffs on imported vehicles.

item.title: German researchers develop AI that predicts liquid properties
item.description:
Artificial intelligence is transforming how scientists study complex physical systems, with recent breakthroughs enabling faster and more accurate simulations of everything from liquid behavior to electron dynamics in water.

Researchers at the University of Bayreuth announced this week a new AI method that can significantly speed up the calculation of liquid properties. Published in the journal Physical Review Letters as an Editors' Suggestion, the approach predicts the chemical potential—a fundamental quantity for describing liquids in thermodynamic equilibrium—without requiring the computationally expensive algorithms traditionally used for such calculations.

item.title: Microbes extract metals from meteorites in space station test
item.description:
A collaborative experiment aboard the International Space Station has demonstrated that microbes can extract valuable platinum-group metals from meteorite material in microgravity, offering a potential pathway for sustainable resource extraction during future deep-space missions.

The BioAsteroid experiment, led by researchers from Cornell University and the University of Edinburgh, tested how a bacterium and a fungus interact with L-chondrite asteroidal material under weightless conditions. NASA astronaut Michael Scott Hopkins conducted the ISS-based portion of the experiment, while scientists performed parallel tests on Earth for comparison.

item.title: DeepMind's Gemini system produces AI-generated research papers
item.description:
Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis envisions humanity standing at the threshold of a transformative era. In a recent interview with Fortune, the Nobel laureate predicted that artificial intelligence will usher in "a kind of new golden era of discovery" within the next 10 to 15 years, fundamentally reshaping medicine, energy, and even space exploration.

"In 10, 15 years' time, we'll be in a kind of new golden era of discovery that is a kind of new renaissance," Hassabis told Fortune Editor-in-Chief Alyson Shontell on the Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry podcast. He described a future of "radical abundance" where AI has "successfully bottled the scientific method" to tackle the planet's most intractable problems.

item.title: AI-physics fusion yields breakthroughs in turbulence and materials
item.description:
A wave of new research demonstrates how artificial intelligence is transforming scientific discovery, from cracking century-old physics problems to speeding up the development of new materials and pharmaceuticals.

In a series of studies published this week, researchers are combining AI with physics-based modeling to tackle problems that have long resisted conventional approaches—offering a blueprint for how machine learning can work alongside human expertise to accelerate breakthroughs.

item.title: US withdraws from al-Tanf base in Syria after nearly a decade
item.description:
American forces have completed their withdrawal from the al-Tanf military base in southeastern Syria, ending nearly a decade of presence at the strategic outpost located at the junction of Syria, Iraq, and Jordan. Syrian government forces have taken control of the facility, marking a turning point in the country's post-Assad transition.

"The American forces withdrew entirely from Al-Tanf base today," a Syrian military source told AFP on February 11. A second source confirmed the withdrawal, adding that US personnel had been moving equipment out of the base for the past 15 days.

The troops have relocated to Tower 22, a facility inside Jordanian territory located approximately 22 kilometers from al-Tanf near the demilitarized zone on the Jordan-Syria border, according to Syrian government sources who spoke to Anadolu Agency. US forces will continue to coordinate with the al-Tanf base from their new position in Jordan.

item.title: Palo Alto lays off hundreds after closing $25B CyberArk deal
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks has finalized its $25 billion acquisition of CyberArk, the largest deal in the cybersecurity company's history, and announced plans to pursue a dual listing on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

The transaction, which closed on Wednesday, establishes identity security as a core pillar of Palo Alto Networks' platform strategy. The company said it intends to integrate CyberArk's identity security platform into its Cortex and Strata platforms to deliver unified protection across human, machine, and artificial intelligence identities.

item.title: Mexican Navy ships deliver aid to Cuba amid U.S. oil blockade
item.description:
Two Mexican Navy ships loaded with more than 800 tons of humanitarian aid docked in Havana on Thursday, delivering food and supplies to an island grappling with a deepening energy crisis fueled by U.S. pressure on Cuba's oil suppliers.

The vessels Papaloapan and Isla Holbox entered Havana Harbor in the morning, according to witnesses from Reuters and AFP, carrying rice, beans, milk, sardines, meat products, canned tuna, vegetable oil, and personal hygiene items. Mexican officials said one ship transported approximately 536 tons of food while the second carried just over 277 tons of powdered milk.

item.title: U.S. covertly sent 6,000 Starlink terminals into Iran, officials say
item.description:
The Trump administration covertly delivered approximately 6,000 Starlink satellite internet terminals into Iran after the regime's violent crackdown on nationwide protests last month, marking the first time the U.S. government has directly sent the technology into the country, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal.

The operation was designed to help Iranian dissidents maintain communications after Tehran severely restricted internet access amid the deadliest wave of unrest in decades.

item.title: Global stocks hit record highs on strong US jobs data
item.description:
Stock markets across Europe and Asia climbed to record highs on Thursday, buoyed by a stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report and upbeat corporate earnings that lifted investor sentiment.

The pan-European STOXX 600 reached an all-time high of 625.86 points, rising 0.7%, with France's CAC 40 leading regional benchmarks with gains exceeding 1.4%, according to Reuters. The rally was driven by strong quarterly results from French firms Legrand and Hermès, with Legrand reporting a 9.6% increase in annual revenue to 9.48 billion euros and adjusted operating profit up 10.5%.

item.title: Russian memo floats return to dollar system in pitch to Trump
item.description:
The Kremlin has drafted an internal memo outlining proposals for sweeping economic cooperation with the United States that includes a return to the dollar system, according to market sources, as Moscow seeks to capitalize on the Trump administration's transactional approach to foreign policy.

The high-level document, drafted this year, identifies seven areas where Russian and American economic interests could align, including cooperation on fossil fuels, joint investments in natural gas and offshore Arctic oil extraction, and opportunities for American companies in critical raw materials. The proposals are contingent on a deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

item.title: Europe overtakes US as Ukraine's largest military backer, study finds
item.description:
Europe has overtaken the United States as Ukraine's largest military backer for the first time since June 2022, according to new data from the Kiel Institute for the World Economy, marking a seismic shift in Western support as the war enters its fifth year.

The German think tank's Ukraine Support Tracker, published on February 11, shows that European nations have now provided €72 billion in total military aid to Kyiv, compared with €65 billion from Washington. The reversal follows a near-total collapse in American support under the Trump administration, with U.S. military aid plummeting 99% in 2025.

item.title: Iran reinforces key nuclear site as US diplomacy continues
item.description:
Fresh satellite imagery reveals Iran is hardening defenses at an underground tunnel complex near Natanz, its most critical remaining nuclear facility, as diplomatic negotiations with the United States continue and military tensions in the region escalate.

Images captured on February 10 by the Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS) show concrete being poured at tunnel entrances and heavy construction equipment actively reinforcing the site at Kolang-Gaz La Mountain, widely known as Pickaxe Mountain, located roughly two kilometers south of the Natanz enrichment facility.

The fortification efforts come eight months after U.S. and Israeli airstrikes struck multiple Iranian nuclear sites during the June 2025 conflict. The United States conducted Operation Midnight Hammer on June 22, 2025, targeting the Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan nuclear facilities with bunker-buster bombs and Tomahawk cruise missiles. Pickaxe Mountain was notably not among the facilities targeted, though analysts say Iran has since accelerated construction there as its most important undamaged nuclear asset.

item.title: Russia dismisses Ukraine claim it can't run Zaporizhzhia plant
item.description:
Ukraine's state nuclear company has warned that a restart of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant under Russian control risks a nuclear accident, prompting a sharp rebuke from Moscow's atomic agency, which dismissed the allegations as unfounded.

Pavlo Kovtoniuk, acting chairman of Energoatom, told Reuters on Tuesday that Russia lacks the necessary equipment and spare parts to safely operate Europe's largest nuclear facility. "Russia will not be able to restart the station. The main equipment and the control, protection, and monitoring systems are all Ukrainian," Kovtoniuk said. "Without spare parts and without the project, the station simply cannot be operated."

item.title: European stocks reverse from record highs as AI fears grip markets
item.description:
European stock markets climbed to fresh all-time highs on Thursday morning as investors cheered positive corporate earnings from luxury and industrial companies, but gains faded later in the session as renewed fears about artificial intelligence disruption dragged global equities lower.

The pan-European STOXX 600 surged 0.7% to 625.86 points in early trading, setting a new record, according to Reuters. France's CAC 40 led regional benchmarks with a 1.4% rise. However, the rally reversed by the close, with the STOXX 600 ending down 0.5% as U.S. markets tumbled, Bloomberg reported.

item.title: Astronomers find 'inside out' solar system with rocky outer planet
item.description:
An international team of astronomers has discovered a planetary system that challenges long-held theories about how planets form, with a rocky world orbiting farther from its star than two gas-rich planets. The discovery, published Wednesday in the journal Science, reveals the first evidence of a planet that may have formed in a gas-depleted environment.

The system orbits LHS 1903, a red dwarf star located 116 light-years from Earth. Using the European Space Agency's CHEOPS satellite, researchers led by Dr. Thomas Wilson of the University of Warwick detected a fourth planet at the system's outer edge—one that unexpectedly appears to be rocky rather than gaseous.

item.title: NASA tests repaired Artemis II rocket after hydrogen leak
item.description: NASA is loading liquid hydrogen into its Space Launch System rocket at Kennedy Space Center on Thursday in a previously unannounced test to verify seal repairs following a leak that halted a critical countdown rehearsal earlier this month. The test marks the latest milestone as the agency works toward launching Artemis II, the first crewed mission to the Moon since the Apollo era.

item.title: Anthropic closes $30B round, valuing AI firm at $380B
item.description:
Anthropic announced Thursday that it has completed a $30 billion Series G funding round, valuing the San Francisco-based AI company at $380 billion post-money. The deal stands as the second-largest private technology fundraise in history, trailing only OpenAI's $40 billion round led by SoftBank in March 2025.

Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC and Coatue Management led the financing, with co-lead investments from D.E. Shaw, Dragoneer Investment Group, Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, ICONIQ, and Abu Dhabi's MGX, according to a GIC press release and Bloomberg reporting. Strategic investors Microsoft and Nvidia, which committed up to a combined $15 billion in Anthropic last November, participated alongside Blackstone, Sequoia Capital, and Altimeter Capital.

item.title: Europe's most powerful rocket launches Amazon satellites in maiden flight
item.description:
Europe's most powerful rocket successfully reached orbit for the first time on Wednesday, carrying 32 satellites for Amazon.com, Inc.'s Leo broadband internet constellation in a launch that marks a new chapter for the continent's space ambitions.

The Ariane 64 lifted off at 16:45 UTC from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, deploying its payload to low-Earth orbit in a mission lasting one hour and 54 minutes. The successful debut flight confirms Europe's heavy-lift launch capability and represents the first commercial customer mission for the Ariane 6 rocket family.
